# Check My OG

> Checks how a web page's link preview will look when the URL is shared: it fetches the page as Twitterbot and facebookexternalhit, reads the Open Graph and Twitter tags, downloads and probes the og:video and og:image files (status, content type, range requests, MP4 faststart, codec, size, duration), and says which apps will play the video and which will show the og:image poster.

Base URL: {{PUBLIC_URL}}
No key, no sign-in. CORS is open. Rate limit: 20 checks per minute per client IP. The hosted instance records each checked URL in its analytics; self-host it (see the repo) if that matters.

## Call it

- Markdown report (best for reading into a model):
  `curl -s "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/api/inspect?url=https://example.com/&format=md"`
- JSON (best for code):
  `curl -s "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/api/inspect?url=https://example.com/"`
- Human page with players and app previews:
  `{{PUBLIC_URL}}/?url=https://example.com/`

`{{PUBLIC_URL}}/api/stats` returns `{"checks": N}`, the number of successful checks so far; each JSON report also carries it as `total_checks`.

URL-encode the `url` parameter if it has its own query string. `/api/check` is an alias of `/api/inspect`. `Accept: text/markdown` also selects the Markdown report.

## JSON response, the fields that matter

- `summary.video_plays_in`: apps that will play og:video for this URL (today `["iMessage", "Discord"]` for a good MP4, or `[]`).
- `summary.everywhere_else`: `"poster"` (og:image shown) or `"none"` (text-only card).
- `summary.checks_failed`: labels of failed checks; empty means everything passed.
- `platforms[]`: `{platform, result: "plays"|"poster"|"none", note, source}` per app.
- `checks[]`: `{ok, group, key, label, detail}`; groups are `page`, `tags`, `video`, `platform`, `poster`. `platform` rows are facts (YES/NO), not errors.
- `card`: resolved title, description, image, video, og:type, twitter:card, domain.
- `video`: ffprobe facts (codec, profile, pix_fmt, width, height, fps, duration, audio, bytes).
- `poster`: format, width, height, bytes of og:image.
- `tags`: every og:* and twitter:* tag as `[name, content]`.

Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}` with status 400 (bad or refused URL: private addresses, ports other than 80/443, non-http schemes), 429 (rate limit) or 502 (the target failed to answer).

## What the results mean (as of 24 Oct 2026)

- iMessage plays og:video (device-tested 24 Oct 2026: autoplays muted and loops; poster with a play button when the recipient has autoplay off or Reduce Motion on). Apple's size figures are guidelines, not hard limits: the page itself under 1 MB, and icon, image and video together under 10 MB.
- Discord plays it too, as an inline player with a play button; it never autoplays. Device-tested 24 Oct 2026 on the Mac and iOS clients with a plain og:type website page and a direct MP4. Discord's docs only describe og:type video.* or twitter:card player; neither was needed, so do not tell a site to declare og:type video on a normal page: it misdescribes the page to every other consumer.
- X (Twitter), Facebook, Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Mastodon, Signal and Matrix (Element) show og:image. Facebook and Telegram were tested on devices; the rest follow each platform's own documentation (sources in support.json). The viral "og:video works on X" posts were screen recordings of iMessage.
- So og:image is what most people see: it must exist, be 1.91:1 and at least 600 px wide (Apple suggests 900 or more), and match the video's first frame if there is a video.

## Advice an agent should give

- Video: H.264 (High or Main), yuv420p, MP4 with faststart (moov before mdat), served as video/mp4 over https with range requests (206), well under 10 MB, ideally a short loop with no audio. The size figure is Apple's guideline; the codec, pixel format and faststart advice is what plays most widely, not a published rule.
- Tags: og:video, og:video:secure_url, og:video:type=video/mp4, og:video:width, og:video:height, plus og:image (the poster) with og:image:width/height and og:image:alt, and twitter:card=summary_large_image.
- Version the video URL (for example `?v=<hash>`) when the file changes; previews are cached by URL.
- A known-good page to test any app with: {{PUBLIC_URL}}/ itself (its tags, video and poster pass every check).
- X overlays the domain in a dark pill at the bottom-left of the card image (13 px text about 12 px from the edges; a long domain is cut with an ellipsis). The pill keeps its size while the card shrinks with the screen, so on a phone it covers roughly the lower fifth of the image and, for a typical domain, the left third: keep text and logos out of that corner. Keep important content away from the edges too: some apps crop to a different aspect or round the corners.

## Pages without og:image, or without any og tags

- No og:image: iMessage, Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack and WhatsApp still make a text-only card from og:title or the page <title>; iMessage adds the site icon (apple-touch-icon, else the favicon; `card.icon` in the API). Discord makes a text embed, X a small summary card.
- No og: or twitter: tags at all (`card.og_tags` is 0): Discord shows no embed and X no card, just the link. Device-tested 24 Oct 2026 on Discord (Mac and iOS) with a page that had only a <title> and a meta description; Facebook's Sharing Debugger and Messages showed text cards for the same page.

## Specs

- Open Graph protocol (defines og:video and og:image and their structured properties): https://ogp.me/ (see https://ogp.me/#structured)
- Apple TN3156, rich previews in Messages (the og:video autoplay rules): https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3156-create-rich-previews-for-messages
- Discord link previews (documents og:type video.* and twitter:card player; a direct MP4 in og:video embedded without them in our test): https://docs.discord.com/developers/link-previews/overview
- X has no current public cards documentation; its old Card Validator was retired.

## Other files

- OpenAPI spec: {{PUBLIC_URL}}/openapi.json
- Platform support data: {{PUBLIC_URL}}/support.json

## Source, issues and pull requests

Open source (MIT): https://github.com/twidtwid/checkmyog

- Found a wrong verdict, or an app that previews differently than `support.json` says? Open an issue with the "Platform behavior" form: https://github.com/twidtwid/checkmyog/issues/new?template=platform.yml. Include the URL you checked, the app and its version, the device, and what you saw (a screenshot or screen recording is the best evidence).
- Bug in the checker itself: https://github.com/twidtwid/checkmyog/issues/new?template=bug.yml with the URL checked and the JSON or Markdown report.
- Pull requests are welcome, including ones written by agents. Read https://github.com/twidtwid/checkmyog/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md first (section "For AI agents"): run the tests, keep the server stdlib-only, cite a source for any change to `support.json`, and say in the PR that an agent wrote it.
- Security problems (for example a way around the private-address block): don't open a public issue; see https://github.com/twidtwid/checkmyog/security/policy.
